destination.name: Tweed Heads
destination.tagline: The northernmost town in New South Wales, on the Queensland border and the Tweed River mouth.
destination.description: At the mouth of the Tweed River, Tweed Heads is the northernmost town in New South Wales and the twin of Coolangatta across the state line. Cedar cutters were the first Europeans to live in the Tweed Valley, in 1844, and the district later turned to dairying, sugar cane, bananas and fishing. Today the draws are the border headlands, the Tweed coast beaches and, about 30 km inland by road, Murwillumbah and the caldera that surrounds Wollumbin. The 1994 film Muriel's Wedding used Tweed Heads as the fictional town of Porpoise Spit.
whyVisit: See Wollumbin rise from the Tweed Valley caldera
Visit the Tweed Regional Gallery and Margaret Olley Art Centre
Ride the Northern Rivers Rail Trail

goodToKnow.title: Wollumbin summit closed
goodToKnow.detail: Wollumbin's summit track is closed, and NPWS will decide its future with Aboriginal custodians. The park stays open for the Lyrebird rainforest walk, picnic areas and camping at Breakfast Creek, so check park alerts before driving out.

goodToKnow.title: Clocks change at the border
goodToKnow.detail: Queensland does not observe daylight saving, so in summer the clocks change an hour across the border from Tweed Heads to Coolangatta. NSW venues such as the Tweed Regional Gallery run on NSW time.

goodToKnow.title: Rail trail logistics
goodToKnow.detail: The rail trail's open Tweed section is 24 km one way, from Murwillumbah Railway Station to Crabbes Creek, so plan a return shuttle or bike hire; the trail website lists both.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Autumn and spring, {months}, are warm and good for walking and riding; humpback whales pass the headlands from June to early November.

tweed-heads-1.bio: The Tweed Shire seat on the Tweed River, with the start of the Northern Rivers Rail Trail, the nearest town to Wollumbin and the Tweed Regional Gallery just outside.

tweed-heads-2.bio: A World Heritage rainforest park around Wollumbin (Mount Warning), the 1,157 m remnant vent of an ancient volcano and a sacred place for the Bundjalung nation; the summit track is closed, but the short Lyrebird track from Mount Warning Road leads to a rainforest lookout.
tweed-heads-2.hours: Daylight; entrance gate may close from 5 PM in winter and 6 PM in summer, reopening at 7 AM

tweed-heads-4.bio: The Captain Cook Memorial Light on the Point Danger headland where the NSW-Queensland border meets the sea, with parkland and sea views (the tower is closed to the public).

tweed-heads-6.bio: A free contemporary art gallery just outside Murwillumbah, home to the Margaret Olley Art Centre, a re-creation of her Sydney workspace, with a guided tour daily at 11:30 am.

tweed-heads-7.bio: A rail trail whose open Murwillumbah to Crabbes Creek section is 24 km, for walkers and riders, with bike hire and shuttles along the way.
tweed-heads-7.hours: Daylight; no set hours (sunrise to sunset recommended)

tweed-heads-8.bio: A surf beach on the Tweed coast with Norries Headland beside it, both popular with visitors, and a good surf break to the north of the headland.
